title: Loops
summary: Repeat code with for and while, build results inside loops, and leave early with break and continue.

concepts.title: Building a result inside a loop

misconceptions.description: Believes a loop with < also runs for the bound, or that a loop with <= stops one pass early.
Believes the update part of a for loop runs before the first pass.
Counts the first pass through a loop as pass zero.
Reads the value a variable has at the end of the program for every earlier step.
Believes the loop condition is checked only after the body has run once.
Believes each pass replaces the result instead of adding to the value it already holds.
Believes a variable declared inside the loop body keeps its value from one pass to the next.
Believes a let inside a loop body is declared again on each pass and causes an error.
Believes break only skips one pass, or that continue ends the whole loop.
Believes break or continue takes effect only after the rest of the pass has run.

conceptCard.title: Repeating with for
conceptCard.body: A for loop repeats a block. Its header has three parts: a start value, a condition checked before every pass, and an update that runs after every pass. When the condition is false, the loop ends.

conceptCard.title: Repeating with while
conceptCard.body: A while loop repeats while its condition is true. The condition is checked before every pass, so the body may never run. Nothing changes the variable for you, so the body must update it.

conceptCard.title: Building a result in a loop
conceptCard.body: To build a result, declare a variable before the loop. Each pass changes it using its old value. After the loop it holds the combined result.

conceptCard.title: break and continue
conceptCard.body: break ends the loop at once. continue skips the rest of the current pass and goes on with the next one. Both are usually placed inside an if.
